details.summary: A comforting, well-designed skillet meal that successfully leverages smart shortcuts to hit the 30-minute promise. However, minor adjustments to the added salt and farro quantities are required to meet the chapter's strict sodium and carbohydrate ceilings.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is highly coherent, relying on classic autumnal pairings. The Dijon mustard and apple cider vinegar provide essential acidity to balance the natural sweetness of the apple and butternut squash.
All listed ingredients are used correctly in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients appear in the steps.
Instructions are well-written, providing accurate cook time ranges, a halfway check for the squash, and clear visual and textural doneness cues.
The recipe perfectly aligns with a Modern American profile, utilizing a familiar mix of pork, orchard fruit, and hearty grains.
The skillet searing followed by a covered simmer works perfectly to brown the meat and then steam-cook the frozen squash and fresh apples evenly.
The computed nutrition values are plausible. The high sodium count makes sense given the combination of added salt, Dijon mustard, and potentially seasoned broth/farro.
The title accurately describes the dish, and the intro sets realistic expectations for a quick, one-pan weeknight meal without relying on any banned health claims.
This recipe sounds delicious and comforting. It offers excellent texture contrast between the soft squash, chewy farro, crisp-tender apple, and wilted spinach.

An excellent example of eating for both conditions simultaneously. It utilizes lean pork, olive oil, a high-quality whole grain, and plenty of produce rather than relying on heavy sauces or refined carbs.
Sweetness comes entirely from whole fruit and vegetables (apple and squash), and the recipe features a robust, high-quality complex carbohydrate base in the farro.

The recipe overshoots the chapter's sodium ceiling (726mg vs 550mg max) and slightly exceeds the carbohydrate ceiling (58g vs 55g max). Fix: Reduce the added salt in the seasoning step from 1/4 tsp to 1/8 tsp (relying on the Dijon for savory punch), and specify 'unseasoned' for the farro pouch while reducing its volume slightly from 7 oz to 5.5 oz to bring carbohydrates back into the target window.
With the smart use of frozen squash and a ready-to-eat farro pouch, prep is minimal. This easily hits the table in under 30 minutes from a cold start, and all ingredients are simple to find.

Skillet searing the pork and using the resulting fond to build a quick pan sauce for the vegetables and grains is a textbook, highly effective cooking method.

A highly appetizing, comforting, and nutrient-dense weeknight dinner that uses accessible flavors beautifully.

Zero added sugar, with natural sweetness elegantly provided by the apple and squash. Carbohydrates are anchored by a high-quality whole grain (farro) and hit the tier window perfectly.
